Package org.aristonis.diwan.database.driver

Interface Driver

All Known Implementing Classes:
AndroidSqliteDriver, JdbcDriver
@Internal public interface Driver
Opens sessions on one database for Diwan Database.

Operations added in later versions arrive as default methods, so an existing driver keeps compiling. A driver has no lifecycle method: shutting down whatever it draws connections from, such as a pool, is the job of whoever owns that pool.

API Note:
Internal: driver SPI for dialect modules.
Implementation Requirements:
Implementations must be safe to call from several threads at once; each call to open() returns a new session that is used by one thread at a time.

  • Method Details

    • open

      DriverSession open()
      Opens a session on one physical connection.
      Returns:
      a new open session, never null; the caller must close it
      Throws:
      DriverException - if no connection can be obtained, including on a timeout
      Implementation Requirements:
      This method may block while waiting for a connection, for example from a pool. A wait that times out must be reported as a DriverException.

    • info

      DriverInfo info()
      Describes the database this driver talks to.
      Returns:
      the database description, never null
      Throws:
      DriverException - if the description cannot be read
      Implementation Requirements:
      This method must be cheap, because the core may call it often. Compute the description once and cache it; any I/O may happen only on the first call.

    • exactDecimalDigits

      default OptionalInt exactDecimalDigits()
      Tells how many significant digits the database stores exactly in a decimal column.
      Returns:
      the number of exact significant digits, or empty when there is no known limit
      Implementation Requirements:
      The default returns empty, meaning no limit is known. A driver for a database that keeps decimals as binary floating point returns the digits it keeps (SQLite: 15).
